question.text: Konark Growth Fund (continued): what is the DPI (Distributions to Paid-In) ratio?

explanation.text: The Logic: DPI = Cumulative Distributions / Capital Called = INR 144 / INR 120 = 1.20x. This measures CASH returned to LPs — the realisation metric. The Trap: A is RVPI; C is TVPI; D is arbitrary. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-A and XIX-C test DPI. LPs benchmark PE/VC GPs on DPI net of carry. Manager's Pro-Tip: DPI > 1.0x means LPs have recovered all their called capital in cash — a psychological milestone. After that, LPs view the remaining TVPI as 'house money' and become more patient on exits. Target DPI > 1.0x by year 6-7 for PE, year 8-9 for VC.
